messages:
maya: Heads-up — saw two ~1m bursts in us-west-2 at 02:13 and 02:18 that completely drained the warm pool and pushed requests into long queueing.  p50 still OK but p95/p99 spiked and admission started rejecting.

raj: Ugh. Any pattern? same model, same size?

maya: both were medium-size text-gen jobs hitting the 8x-GPU pool for 'gpt-xxl-8q'. workload had a lot of short sessions with sudden fan-out. autoscaler scaled but warm startup lagged ~45-70s so admission ramped up rejects first.

olivia: do we have metrics for "warm-pool utilization" vs start latency? want to know if the pool sizing or cooldowns are the issue.

maya: yes — chart I pulled: warm_pool_capacity=8, active=8 -> preemptive start queue=12 -> avg cold-start=62s when new instance needed. cooldown window is 120s. attaching snippet of the config we ran in prod: ```yaml
preprovision:
  warm_pool: 8
  cooldown_s: 120
admission:
  token_bucket:
    rate: 100/s
    burst: 250
```

david: two levers here: reduce cold-starts by increasing warm_pool (cost), or smooth incoming admission so we don't blow the burst. we should also consider adaptive warm pool: grow warm pool when short-term in-flight > threshold and shrink after longer quiet.

raj: agree. propose adaptive rules: - if queue_length_1m > 10 AND p95_latency > 600ms => warm_pool += 4 (cap 32) - cooldown for shrink only after 10m quiet. this avoids thrash.

olivia: sounds good. what about admission changes? token bucket fixed burst already allows big fanouts to flood. We could tie burst to available warm instances: burst = base_burst + available_warm * per_instance_burst.

maya: yeah example formula: `burst = 100 + max(0, available_warm - reserved) * 20`. So when warm drop to 0, burst drops to base and we stop allowing big floods.

david: we should also add gradual ramping heuristic: when a new warm node is provisioning, hold per-client concurrency to 2 until warm node is ready. That reduces pressure on admission and ensures clients backoff instead of retrying full blast.

olivia: any thoughts on cost impact? increasing warm_pool by 4 in that AZ is ~+18% cost for that capacity tier during peak hours. But rejects and p99 latency are worse for customer experience. need tradeoff doc.

raj: for short-term mitigation: tweak token_bucket rate up slightly for high-tier customers and lower for free tier during burst windows. also add capacity-aware burst per canyon.

sre-bot: Incident note: us-west-2 warm-pool drain detected at 02:13, 02:18. Auto-scaler triggered new nodes at 02:14 and 02:19. Observed admission rejects: 64 -> 12.

maya: proposed immediate action items: 1) implement adaptive warm_pool scaling rule (fast grow slow shrink) 2) change admission burst to depend on available_warm 3) add per-client concurrency clamp during provisioning 4) dashboard for warm_pool headroom and cold-start latency.

deploy-bot: Canary plan queued: scale-smoothing-preprovisioning v1 -> rollout to us-west-2 canary (5% traffic) at 03:10 UTC.

david: I'll draft the admission change PR and include the burst formula + unit tests.

maya: I'll own the adaptive warm_pool controller and dashboard panels.

olivia: I'll model cost delta for +4 warm nodes over 24/7 vs peak-hours-only. will post numbers in the runbook. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

raj: assign me to validate canary behavior and prepare rollback knobs. if canary looks good we flip to 50% after 1h.

maya: cool. follow-up: add a low-overhead experiment to sample client retry/backoff behavior so we don't punish legitimate spikes.

david: ack. will add small telemetry flag to track per-client retry timing.

maya: thanks all. will update thread with PR links and dashboard URLs once available. :thumbsup:
